issues.issue: Did the officer fetter his discretion by treating the pending spousal sponsorship application as not imminent?
issues.applicant_position: Officer imposed an arbitrary limit on deferral duration by finding the pending sponsorship decision not imminent.
issues.result_quote: Having regard to all of the foregoing, the Officer cannot be said to have fettered his discretion

issues.issue: Are the arguments on Ms. Taylor's high-risk pregnancy and post-partum period still live?
issues.applicant_position: Officer's treatment of high-risk pregnancy and post-partum support was unreasonable.
issues.result_quote: the issues that Mr. Forde has raised in respect of the Officer’s treatment of Ms. Taylor’s pregnancy and her post-partum period are now moot

issues.issue: Did the officer unreasonably assess Ms. Taylor's mental and physical health evidence?
issues.applicant_position: Officer unreasonably dealt with evidence of Ms. Taylor's long-term mental health struggle and chronic foot pain.
issues.result_quote: the Officer’s treatment of the issues that Mr. Forde raised with respect to Ms. Taylor’s mental and physical health was not unreasonable.

issues.issue: Did the officer unreasonably assess the best interests of the children and stepchildren?
issues.applicant_position: Assessment flawed: no particularized analysis per child, unreasonable speculation about transition and visits.
issues.result_quote: the Officer’s treatment of the submissions made by Mr. Forde in respect of the best interests of his children did not result in his decision being unreasonable.

issues.issue: Did the officer unreasonably assess the personal hardship the applicant would face in Jamaica?
issues.applicant_position: Officer speculated and failed to appreciate the nature of hardships he would face in Jamaica.
issues.result_quote: it was not unreasonable for the Officer to have failed to have given greater weight or consideration to those factors
